name: The Smallest String Concatenation
description: You're given a list of n strings a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . You'd like to concatenate them together in some order such that the resulting string would be lexicographically smallest. Given the list of strings, output the lexicographically smallest concatenation.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n — the number of strings ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10 4 ). Each of the next n lines contains one string a i ( 1 ≤ | a i | ≤ 50 ) consisting of only lowercase English letters. The sum of string lengths will not exceed 5·10 4 .
output_specification: Print the only string a — the lexicographically smallest string concatenation.
subsubtopic: 406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton
approach_summary: Precompute the prefix function π[i] matching longest proper prefix-suffix in O(M). Traverse text string with π transitions to locate all occurrences in O(N) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 632C — The Smallest String Concatenation [406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton]
topic_editorial.summary: String matching with prefix automaton / KMP.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The prefix function $\pi[i]$ defines the length of the longest proper prefix of $S[0..i]$ that is also a suffix of $S[0..i]$. When a mismatch occurs at index $j$, we do not backtrack in text; we jump to $\pi[j-1]$, preserving previously matched characters.
